qualification: Audit metadata only. Handwritten registrations remain the only execution route; the runtime never loads this file, review.json or any ledger to grant a request.
limitations: No authenticated-cloud, paid or release acceptance; every operation stays cloud-unverified.

The complete reviewed batch-B twenty is typed: batch A ten, batch B1 ten configuration operations, batch B2 seven domain/public-policy operations and batch B3 three Sippy operations; the credential operation stays DEFERRED_PENDING_APPROVAL outside batch B.

Sippy semantics: a GET never restores secret keys (the provider only echoes public metadata); a PUT receipt proves only that the configuration was accepted, never that the keys work, that a migration ran or that a connection succeeded.
An UNKNOWN/ACCEPTED/PARTIAL Sippy PUT is never promoted to SUCCEEDED by observing identical public metadata, and no write is ever replayed.
A Sippy DELETE only proves the configuration is known-disabled; it never deletes objects already copied.
Five controlled jurisdictions are the only ones admitted, and only for the reviewed operations that declare the header; the same bucket group lock serialises A/B1/B2/B3.

A REST account-level grant is required for Sippy writes: an S3 key or bucket-item permission is not administration, and the actual one-use editor material/random binding cannot be rebuilt from audit metadata.
